findings.reason: as written the codex-anchored verdict is structurally undecidable, so the plan needs either a codex replicate in §14 or a stated reason for judging a codex difference against a clive spread.
findings.text: "its paired 90% interval is separated from the same-arm spread (the clive replicate paired with clive)" is the separation test for every treatment, including codex-anchored, whose baseline is codex; §14's own committed record reads that spread as 0.06M to 7.97M with a +4.01M point estimate against a clive baseline mean of 19.39M, and reports codex-anchored's −8.01M to 1.48M interval as "overlaps the same-arm interval, so the arm is not separated" even though its saving is 37.5% of a codex baseline that spends about 8.4M — a yardstick taken from an arm that spends more than twice as much, and one whose lower bound sits just above zero, so a codex treatment can never clear it however well it does

findings.reason: a worker closing the section on an adopted omp-local cannot state what it wrote, and the record's "verdict per treatment" has no matching action for one of five arms.
findings.text: the completion write is "the flight default for `anchored_edit` per backend follows the verdict: an adopted treatment's default is turned on, and every other treatment's default stays off", but the omp-local arm is a backend and a dialect, not an `anchored_edit` flag (the same paragraph's removal clause names "the `omp` dialect, its `_HARNESS_HOME` entry and the `omp-local` backend"), so an adopted omp-local has no flag to turn on and "every other treatment's default stays off" assigns it a default that does not exist

findings.reason: a declared edge is what holds a queue at the upstream, and this section's measure can only be taken once those replays exist, so the dependency the section states is missing from the wiring that enforces it.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` for `s8` names s4, s5, s7 and s10 only, while s8's new Deliverable makes §14's committed assignments the entire verdict population and states its node is dispatched only "after every replay of every committed assignment has a recorded verdict"; neither s14 nor s13 appears in the edge set, so the one gate the section now depends on is prose alone

findings.reason: the containing directory is a durable path the node can glob and the node reads code, so a naming convention is a brief detail rather than a change to what counts as done.
findings.text: an extension is "committed beside the first assignment" with no filename, while the node must pool "over every replayed section" of every committed assignment

The new s17 adds the codex replicate as a seventh arm of the extension, so codex has a yardstick of its own.
